name: Rouran Khaganate
summary: A nomadic confederation on the Mongolian steppe that rivalled the Northern Wei of China, and the first to use the title khagan, until the Göktürks overthrew it in 552–555.

knownFor.label: Title “khagan”
knownFor.note: The Rouran were the first to call their ruler khagan, later used by Turks and Mongols.

knownFor.label: Mounted archers
knownFor.note: Steppe cavalry that raided northern China.

knownFor.label: Yurt camps
knownFor.note: Felt tents of a mobile people.

location.value: All of modern Mongolia and Inner Mongolia, plus parts of Manchuria, eastern Siberia, Xinjiang and Kazakhstan.

terrain.value: Wide grasslands, the Gobi Desert to the south, and the Altai and Khangai mountains to the west.

climate.value: Very continental: bitterly cold winters, short warm summers and little rain, with harsh winter storms (dzud).

resources.value: Pasture, horses, iron from subject peoples.

disasters.value: Harsh winters and droughts that killed herds; Chinese records mention famines among the Rouran.

population.value: Not stated; the page says the state was undoubtedly multi-ethnic.

urbanisation.value: No towns of their own; people lived in mobile camps, though they controlled oasis cities such as Turfan at times.

disease.value: Unknown; few records survive. Livestock diseases and harsh winters probably mattered most.

migration.value: Northern Wei campaigns pushed Rouran groups north and west; after 552 survivors fled to China, and some may have gone west.

economicBase.value: Controlled trade routes and raided oasis towns such as Gaochang; the state aimed at requisitioning surplus products from neighbours. Herding appears only in a quoted Chinese account.

tradeRoutes.value: Silk Road routes north of China; they traded horses and furs to China and took tribute from the Turfan oasis.

wealth.value: Wealth came from tribute, raids on China and control of subject peoples and oasis trade.

moneyAndTax.value: No coinage of their own; wealth was counted in herds, and subject peoples paid tribute in livestock, iron and goods.

inequality.value: Khagan and nobles above herders and subject peoples.

governmentType.value: An imperial confederation under a khagan, with a kurultai as its assembly.

keyRulers.value: Yujiulü Shelun united the Rouran clans around 402; Anagui was the last great khan and killed himself after defeat.

succession.value: Within the ruling Yujiulü clan; brothers and sons often fought over the throne.

institutions.value: Tribal chiefs and councils under the khagan; military units organised by tribe.

stability.value: Frequent internal conflict and defeats by the Northern Wei; the realm split several times in the 400s and 500s.

eliteConflict.value: Rival royal princes; in 520 the khagan Anagui fled to the Northern Wei before returning to power.

armyAndTech.value: Mounted archers and lancers, organised into units of a thousand and a hundred, like later steppe armies.

majorWars.value: Perpetual conflict with Northern Wei, which launched a major offensive in 429; Göktürk rebels defeated the Rouran in 552.

territoryChange.value: Defeated by the Göktürks under Bumin (552), after which the khaganate quickly collapsed.

alliancesRivals.value: Allied at times with southern Chinese dynasties against Wei.

inventions.value: Few known inventions; they may have spread the title khagan and some steppe customs to later peoples.

scienceEducation.value: No writing of their own is known; Chinese records say they used tally sticks to count.

openness.value: Contacts with China, Central Asian oases and the Hephthalites through trade, marriage alliances and war.

communicationTransport.value: Horses for riding and messages, and ox-drawn wagons for moving felt tents and families between pastures.

religion.value: Tengrism, shamanism and Buddhism (infobox); a shaman figurine was found in a princess’s tomb.

artsArchitecture.value: Little survives; probably felt, leather, metal horse gear and gold ornaments like other steppe peoples.

socialStructure.value: Ruling clan, nobles, herders, subject tribes.

sharedIdentity.value: Loyalty to the khagan and the ruling clan rather than to one people; many tribes were subjects.

dailyLife.value: Herding families lived in felt tents, moving with the seasons and eating meat and milk from sheep, horses and cattle.

neighbours.value: The Northern Wei and later Northern Qi in China, the Göktürks in the Altai, the Gaoche (Tiele) tribes and the Hephthalites.

ideasReligions.value: Spread the title khagan, later used by the Göktürks, Avars and others.

colonisation.value: None; they ruled subject tribes such as the Türks and Gaoche through tribute rather than by settlement.

riseSignals.value: The infobox gives 330; Shelun united the Rouran in 402 and took the title Qiudoufa Khagan (reigned 402–410). The Rouran were the first people to use the titles khagan and khan.

peakPeriod.value: The early 400s under Shelun and his successors, when they ruled most of the Mongolian steppe.

declineSignals.value: Revolt of the Göktürks, their former iron-working subjects.

outcome.value: The Rouran were said to be at the peak of their might shortly before the Turks defeated them in 552; Turks invaded in 555 and Muqan annihilated them.
